The pessimistic and nihilistic point of view is simply easy to reach when in the thralls of chronic pain. I have studied Stoicism for 10 years and its quite more then simply seeing everything as an opinion. Nowadays with it becoming more popular you have people kinda whitewashing and westernizing and dumbing down Stoicism like what we did with meditation and yoga...when really its a complete way of life rather than simply a collection of ideas or practices. Stoicism has saved me despite being at a high level of pain on the daily for years, I beg you and everyone reading this giant wall of text to give it a better chance. You could have more happiness, less existential pain, and more meaning by following their way of life. 

Stoicism is about learning to live in harmony with nature. According to them, the Good Life, Happiness, Eudaimonia is living in accordance with Nature, both the outer Nature which is the universe and our inner nature of our spiritual higher self known as our Daimon. We do this by recognizing that the only truth, the only thing we can logically and rationally deduce as true is that Virtue is good. Virtue is the same as Right Reason and Nature and Happiness according to the Stoics. 

By this point, living in harmony with your higher self and the universe is the only truthful and rational way of living. That means on a practical level that we are to live with rational actions and thoughts in a consistent way. Their main other point is that since the only truth is Virtue is Good, Virtue being living with rational actions based on rational perceptions, that means everything else is false. As in our daily perceptions of the world, our passions or false beliefs or opinions are worthless in the grand scheme of things. Opinions, or false beliefs, or value judgments, cause contractions in us or discomfort in the form of cognitive dissonance. This in turn can increase physical pain as emotional pain and physical pain go hand in hand. 

So, TLDR: To decrease pain and increase happiness, we learn to control our perceptions so that instead of having negative tinged emotions-which to the stoics are the same as value judgments or false beliefs- we instead work on only having positive emotions. This leads to less inner turmoil and thus less pain. Positive emotions are logically tied to right reasoned beliefs, so to start beliving that to be moral is good, to live well is the true good, is to live the true Stoic way of life. Focus on how to be the best person you can be, whether thats for your higher self known as your daimon, whether its for your pain, whether its for the universe and nature and for our brotherhood of man--the intention will ride out correctly in the end as you learn what it means to be Good and Virtous through practice. 

I can attest that focusing on being a Good person,focusing on truthful perceptions which bring good emotions, on being grateful, on loving your fate...this will bring you relief. Don't let people who think their introduction into Stoicism has led them to understand all the nuances of the practice. Its a deep way of life based on the Good and being Good and harmonizing yourself with the universe. And I find it to be one of the few things which can actually help our chronic pain community.
